title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az peering + route53 + sgs + interface endpoints
author: Sanjay Rao
description: Motivation: add production-ready Terraform modules and installer hooks for provisioning Redwood Private control plane networking across multiple AZs with VPC peering, Route53 cross-account delegation, interface endpoints and hardened security groups. This change unifies previous ad-hoc scripts, supports cross-account peering for customer-managed VPCs, and introduces upgrade/rollback hooks used by the private-installer to migrate networking during upgrades. What changed: 1) terraform/modules/control-plane-vpc: new multi_az submodule (private_subnets, nat_gateways optional, subnet CIDR allocation by AZ), 2) terraform/modules/peering: cross-account peering resource set with lifecycle rules and route table propagation, 3) terraform/modules/route53-delegation: conditional creation of hosted zone delegation records and IAM role wiring for cross-account DNS updates, 4) terraform/modules/interface-endpoints: configurable interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/ECR with security group scoping, 5) private-installer: installer hooks (pre-upgrade networking-check, post-upgrade rollback-snapshot) and CLI flags to toggle automated peering, 6) helm/redwood-private: chart values updated to accept peering IDs and Route53 delegation ARNs, 7) docs/installer/networking.md: new operations guide and rollback instructions. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous single-AZ behavior; automated peering is opt-in via installer flag --auto-peer. Upgrade considerations: the installer will create peering connections in a non-blocking canary mode by default and annotate Kubernetes CRs with peering state; full traffic cutover requires operator confirmation. Rollback: post-upgrade hook captures route table and security group snapshots to permit automated rollback if a later step fails. Testing and validation: - unit: terraform validate for each module; - integration: terratest scenario that provisions a 2-AZ control plane in a sandbox account and verifies route propagation and DNS delegation; - e2e: private-installer end-to-end run with dry-run and confirm mode. Security: SGs are locked down to only control-plane subnets and peering CIDRs; audit logs are produced for all IAM/Route53 changes. Related: Linear ENG-1024, INF-88; support ticket SUP-3421. Release notes: Adds multi-AZ VPC provisioning for the private control plane with optional automated cross-account peering and Route53 delegation. Operators should read docs/installer/networking.md before enabling auto-peering.
